Pick the next species

Three concepts built around the idea-pool themes: drawbacks, conversions and rule-breaking. Two hunter-style drafts each; tap a thumbnail to swap the portrait. All numbers are placeholders.

Mirage Moth (sprite) is already light in species.csv, so Candlemane would be the second light species, not the first. It is designed as the moth’s opposite.

Candlemane

LightMythic

A sacred lion of living candle wax. Its mane is a ring of votive candles and it burns its own body to shine.

Self-burning HP/WIS bruiser. The survival stats are its damage; lowest DEF on purpose.

Native trees

  • Votive Flame HP tree. Skill Votive Strike (costs 5% max HP). Capstone reuses lane A blood_magic: no cooldowns, each cast costs HP.
  • Sanctum Grace WIS tree. Skill Halo Mend (self heal). Capstone trigger: when hit, cast Halo Mend at 50%.

Chase capstones

In-runMartyr’s Pyre

martyr_flame: every heal also deals 60% of the amount as light damage; overheal converts at 100%.

Apex: Martyr Pyrelion
BookHollow Sun

hollow_sun (book: Psalter of the Unburnt): HP paid or lost is stored as Radiance; each hit releases 25% as damage and heals half of it.

Apex: Hollow Sun Lion

Why it plays differently

The only species that wants to lose HP: pay HP, heal, turn the heal into damage. DEF drills are the wrong plan. Slow, heavy opposite of the fast, fragile Mirage Moth.

Needs lane A (blood_magic).

Pyre Stag

FireGrimdark

A gaunt ash-grey stag whose antlers are its own funeral pyre, hung with penitent chains and black bells.

Glass-cannon STR/INT hybrid on a fuse. HP is fuel; DEF growth 0.5, the lowest in the game.

Native trees

  • Funeral Pyre Skill Immolate (fire nuke, costs 5% max HP). Capstone pyre_tithe: pay 5% max HP per action; damage ×(1 + missing HP%), up to about ×2.
  • Ashen Vigil Skill: shield. Capstone ash_shroud: at fight start, turn 25% of HP into a shield, so low-HP rules (vantage, resentment) switch on early.

Chase capstones

In-runInverted Mercy

pyre_mercy: it can never be healed. Every heal it would get is dealt as fire damage instead, so generic heal trees become nukes.

Apex: Cinder Saint
BookUndying Pyre

ember_eternal (book: Litany of Embers): lethal damage burns max HP instead, +1.5% damage per 1% burned; dies below 30% of starting max HP.

Apex: Everpyre Hart

Why it plays differently

Training is inverted: drill HP as fuel, skip DEF. Its capstones break rules instead of adding numbers, and it is a hub for lane A/B trees.

Needs lanes A and B. Overlaps Candlemane’s “burn HP” theme.

Cuckling

DarkCute, wrong edge

A round, fluffy cuckoo chick too big for its thorny nest, wearing a stolen eggshell. The egg it pushed out lies beside it.

LUK/SPD tempo thief: wins by taking turns and fielding extra units, not by hitting hard.

Native trees

  • Nest Thief SPD/LUK tree, skill coin_toss. Capstone stolen_turn: once per enemy per fight, with gauge ≥ 50% it acts in the enemy’s place and the enemy loses its turn.
  • Brood Nest Capstone reuses lane F mimic_core: copies the capstone of the tree before it. Pays off only after you overwrite your own Nest Thief: the cuckoo pushes out its sibling.

Chase capstones

In-runUsurped Nest

usurp: each stolen turn casts the victim’s own best skill back at its side and puts it on cooldown.

Apex: Usurper Cuckoo
BookClutch Throne

foundling_egg (book: The Foundling’s Ledger): lays an egg at fight start even on a full side (1v1 becomes 2v1); it hatches into a half-strength Foundling.

Apex: Clutch Empress

Why it plays differently

Breaks turn order and team size instead of raising a stat. Its two native trees work against each other, so every run forks: keep the nest (Usurper) or evict it (Empress).

Needs lanes C, E, F. 5th unit in PvP 4v4 is your call.
